44.0.0.en: 1 “And now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen: 2 Thus saith the LORD that made thee, and formed thee from the womb, which will help thee: Fear not, O Jacob, my servant; and thou, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen. 3 For I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring: 4 And they shall spring up as among the grass, as willows by the water courses. 5 One shall say, I am the LORD’S; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the LORD, and surname himself by the name of Israel.”

44.0.1.en: God fulfills His calling and choosing of the new Israel by the outpouring of His Holy Spirit upon the believers to establish the Church of the New Testament, for He says: “And now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen: Thus saith the LORD that made thee, and formed thee from the womb, which will help thee: Fear not, O Jacob, my servant; and thou, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen. For I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring: and they shall spring up as among the grass, as willows by the water courses. One shall say, I am the LORD’S; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the LORD, and surname himself by the name of Israel” [1-5].

44.0.2.en: In this great gift the following is noted:

44.0.3.en: a. God longs to give not only His outward blessings and gifts but to give Himself to man: “I will pour my spirit upon thy seed”; the Giver of gifts and the Bestower of blessing gives Himself as a gift and a present...

44.0.4.en: * He who is washed for salvation receives the water and the Holy Spirit.

44.0.5.en: Origen * (The baptized) receives the Holy Spirit within him and truly bears the title of temple of God.

44.0.6.en: St. Cyril the Great * O Only-begotten One, who gave us His Spirit in Baptism, give me a word that I may chant to You with love.

44.0.7.en: * The only-begotten Son came down and raised you from the dunghill and gave you His Spirit in Baptism and made you His brother.

44.0.8.en: * We were naturalized into His divinity within the waters, and became sons in truth, and from that time it has been ours to call Him our Father, that hidden One who gave us His Spirit in Baptism.

44.0.9.en: Mar Jacob of Serugh considers this gift of God to be the greatest, for it is He who in His love formed us, and from the womb helped us, and here He demands of us not to fear because He chose us, and to accomplish this choosing He gave us this gift.

44.0.10.en: b. He calls His Church “Jeshurun,” and this name appeared four times in the Old Testament (Deut 32:15; 33:5-6), its meaning being “upright,” derived from yashar. It is as though He calls His Church, which has included sinners, “upright,” and that by the work of His Holy Spirit. It is as though He encourages His people to respond to the gift of His Holy Spirit so that they leave their deviation and disobedience and sing of the splendor of the Lord and His spiritual beauty.

44.0.11.en: For in the Song of Songs, while the Church confesses that trials have darkened her (Song 1:6), yet God the Bridegroom and Savior never hinted at any fault in her, but on the contrary brings out all the beauty in her: “Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves’ eyes” (Song 1:15), “Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee” (Song 4:7).

44.0.12.en: The Lord Christ sees in His Church a surpassing beauty whose secret is the two dove eyes, for the Holy Spirit, who appears in the form of a dove, has come down upon her, granting her spiritual enlightenment. Origen says: [Her eyes are compared to doves surely because she has now come to understand the Holy Scriptures according to the Spirit and not according to the letter. She has come to perceive the spiritual mysteries in the Holy Scriptures, for the dove is a symbol of the Holy Spirit. When we understand the Law and the Prophets in a spiritual way we have the two dove eyes. Therefore in the Book of Psalms her soul longed to have the wings of a dove (Ps 55:6), that she might be able to fly to the understanding of the spiritual mysteries and rest in the courts of wisdom]. As for St. Gregory of Nyssa, he sees that the secret of the Church’s beauty is her dove eyes, for they are pure, and in them appears the image of the Holy Spirit, upon whom the Bride gazes continually, so that His image is imprinted on the pupil of the eye.

44.0.13.en: St. Jerome sees that the secret of the Church’s beauty is her union with the only-begotten Son of God, so that she bears His glory within her, for he says: [What is more beautiful than the soul that is called a daughter of God (Ps 45:10), that does not seek outward adorning (1 Pet 3:3)?! She believes in Christ, and since His Spirit is given to her she takes her way toward Christ, who is at the same time her Bridegroom and her Lord, with great hope].

44.0.14.en: c. He presents to us the gift of His Holy Spirit, who works in us according to our need; for whoever is thirsty, He pours water for him to quench his thirst, and whoever is like dry ground, He pours out upon him floods so that dryness and desert are turned into a garden. He is generous in giving, giving us according to our need and the measure of our response to Him. He says: “Open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it” (Ps 81:10).

44.0.15.en: * Whatever flame the Spirit kindles within us we can, if we wish, make blaze more and more, and if we do not wish we lose it at once (by our slackness and our lack of response to Him).

44.0.16.en: St. John Chrysostom * Those who receive Him (the Holy Spirit) enjoy Him according to their capacity, not according to what He is able.

44.0.17.en: St. Basil the Great * You are receiving military equipment against the power of the enemy (Satan)... Behold the weapon is prepared: the sword of the Spirit (Eph 6:17). It is ready, so it befits you to stretch out your right hand in a good way, that you may fight the battle of the Lord and overcome the opposing powers and become an impregnable (fortress) that repels every attempt of the heretics...

44.0.18.en: * Do not despise grace because it is free, but receive it and treasure it with piety.

44.0.19.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem d. What does it mean: “they shall spring up as among the grass, as willows by the water courses”? Perhaps He meant that he who enjoys the gift of the Holy Spirit grows like a huge tree among perishing grass.

44.0.20.en: e. He who enjoys the Spirit writes on his hand: “For the Lord”; for the ancient custom was that a man would write the name of his god or master on his hand as a tattoo, and God forbade His people from doing so, lest they write the name of the idol on their hands when they deviated, so that it would be difficult, indeed impossible, to remove.

44.0.21.en: “And surname himself by the name of Israel,” for the Church of the New Testament, which enjoys the gift of the Spirit, bore the title “the new Israel”; she inherited from the old Israel the Holy Scriptures with what they contain of divine law and commandments and prophecies and covenants and promises... She understood all that by the Spirit and not the letter and perceived divine mysteries and enjoyed surpassing things.

44.1.0.en: 6 Thus saith the LORD the King of Israel, and his redeemer the LORD of hosts: “I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God. 7 And who is like me? Let him call, and let him declare it and set it before me, since I appointed the ancient people. And the things that are coming, and shall come, let them shew unto them. 8 Fear ye not, neither be afraid: have not I told thee from that time, and have declared it? ye are even my witnesses. Is there a God beside me? Nor any rock that I know not of?”

44.1.1.en: The speaker here is the Lord Christ, the Rock that poured forth water for the people (1 Cor 10:4), therefore He says “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty” [3]; and here He calls Himself “the King of Israel, and his redeemer” [6], and He confessed before Pilate that He is a king.

44.1.2.en: He calls Himself here “the LORD of hosts,” “I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God” [6]. And in the Book of Revelation the Lord Christ says: “I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending” (Rev 1:8), “I am the first and the last” (Rev 1:17; 22:13). It is clear that the Redeemer, the LORD of hosts, the only God beside whom there is no other God, is Christ the Savior... This is the testimony of those who enjoy His salvation: “Ye are even my witnesses. Is there a God beside me?!” [8].

44.2.0.en: What we enjoy in the New Testament is an extension of the continuing work of God; the God who worked with the ancient people [7] had declared to them beforehand the things to come, that is, what He had planned for the sake of the New Testament [7].

44.2.1.en: Perhaps He presented Himself here as “the first and the last” to declare that He Himself who worked in the old is still the same One who works in the New Testament.

44.2.2.en: God the Savior is the first and the last: He goes before all the ranks to lead His flock and comes behind them to support every slow or weak sheep... He embraces all and has compassion on all. He is also the first as the Head of the Church and the last as He became the servant of all. We find Him the first and the last in our lives, satisfying all our needs, so that we lack nothing!

44.3.0.en: 9 They that fashion an idol are all of them vanity, and their delectable things shall not profit; and their witnesses are they; it seeth not, nor knoweth; that they may be ashamed. 10 Who hath formed a god, or molten a graven image that is profitable for nothing? 11 Behold, all his fellows shall be ashamed: and the workmen, they are of men. They are all gathered together, they stand up; they fear, and they shall be ashamed together. 12 The smith hath wrought iron into an axe, and worketh in the coals, and with hammers he fashioneth it, and worketh it with the strength of his arm: yea, he is hungry, and his strength faileth: he hath drunk no water, and is faint. 13 The carpenter hath hewn wood; he stretcheth out the line; he marketh it out with an awl, he maketh it with chisels, and he marketh it out with the compass, and maketh it after the figure of a man, according to the beauty of a man; that it may remain in the house! 14 He hath hewn him down cedars, and taken the cypress and the oak, and chosen for himself among the trees of the forest. He planteth an ash, and the rain doth nourish it. 15 Then it becometh for a man to burn: for he taketh thereof, and warmeth himself; yea, he kindleth it, and baketh bread; then he maketh a god, and worshippeth it! He hath made it a graven image, and falleth down thereto. 16 He burneth part thereof in the fire; with part thereof he eateth flesh; he roasteth roast, and is satisfied! yea, he warmeth himself, and saith, “Aha, I am warm, I have seen the fire.” 17 And the residue thereof he hath made a god, a graven image for himself! He falleth down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and saith, “Deliver me; for thou art my god.” 18 They know not, nor understand: for their eyes are smeared, that they cannot see; and their hearts, that they cannot understand. 19 And none considereth in his heart, neither is there knowledge nor understanding to say, “I have burned part of it in the fire; yea, I have baked bread also upon the coals thereof; I have roasted flesh, and eaten it: and shall I make the residue thereof an abomination? shall I fall down to the stock of a tree?” 20 He feedeth on ashes: a deceived heart hath led him astray, that he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, “Is there not a lie in my right hand?”

44.3.1.en: After speaking of the great gift of the Spirit, which presented us as witnesses for the truth, we declare our enjoyment of God our Savior as the LORD of hosts, the leader of the spiritual battle, and the One who satisfies all as the First and the Last, the support of the men of the Old Testament and also of the believers of the New Testament... Now He compares the testimony of the believers with the testimony of the idol-worshippers:

44.3.2.en: a. Witness to the Savior grants satisfaction and quenching of thirst and fruitfulness: “For I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground... and they shall spring up as among the grass, as willows” [3, 4], while witness to idols offers vanity and emptiness and hunger with blindness and ignorance: “They that fashion an idol are all of them vanity, and their delectable things shall not profit; and their witnesses are they; it seeth not, nor knoweth; that they may be ashamed” [9].

44.3.3.en: Our Christ satisfies the depths, in Him is all sufficiency; those who have experienced Him have felt satisfied and lacked nothing at all; but outside Him is the loss of all inner satisfaction and the deprivation of enjoyment of fellowship with God, the source of life and satisfaction.

44.3.4.en: b. Witness to the Savior grants peace: “Fear not” [2]; “Fear ye not, neither be afraid” [8], but outside Him is fear and trembling: “They are all gathered together, they stand up; they fear, and they shall be ashamed together” [11]. All the energies were gathered together against Him: chief priests and scribes and Pharisees and Sadducees and Roman governors, etc... yet they carried terror and fear even in the moments of the crucifixion and the mocking of the Crucified One! Their inner evil terrified them and the emptiness of their hearts of divine grace, and nature rose up against them, so the sun was darkened and the moon was eclipsed and earthquakes occurred and the rocks were rent and many of the dead arose!

44.3.5.en: c. The Lord’s witnesses enjoy honor, being counted “the new Israel,” and they engrave the name of the Savior on their inner hands, as though they do nothing except in His name [5]; but the witnesses of those outside Him carry shame and disgrace [11].

44.4.0.en: He presents to us a wonderful portrayal of the corruption of idol worship, showing that the idols and their makers and those who worship them all carry shame and vanity. The makers of idols are earnest, not caring for hunger or thirst or weariness [12] in order to make the axe of iron and to beat out plates to set up images. So also the carpenters who spend every effort to carve wooden images... All of them labor and do not tire to set up images of metal or wood unable to offer salvation, while the children of God are lax in their spiritual striving despite their enjoyment of divine possibilities able to bring them to enjoy eternal salvation. It is as though these workers of vanity condemn the lax children of God, as the Lord of glory Jesus said that the sons of this generation are wiser than the sons of the Kingdom (Lk 16:8).

44.4.1.en: On the other hand, the making of metal images exhausts the energy of the makers, while the making of wooden images is accompanied by amusement with the remaining wood, as it is used in the hearth for warmth or for cooking food, at the same time that they soothe their conscience by worshipping the wood carved as an image.

44.4.2.en: Finally, what does idol worship (= withdrawal from God) offer:

44.5.0.en: a. Blindness of inner insight and inner darkness [18], while Christ is the Sun of righteousness (Mal 4:2).

44.5.1.en: b. Ignorance and lack of knowledge [9], while Christ is our righteousness.

44.6.0.en: c. Hunger, so that man eats ashes [20], while the Lord Christ is the heavenly Bread.

44.6.1.en: d. Falsehood, deceit and misleading [20], while the Lord Christ is the way and the truth.

44.6.2.en: In other words, we find in our Christ inner enlightenment and knowledge and satisfaction and truth and all our needs, but outside Him there is nothing but inner emptiness and a sense of isolation and the loss of inner insight.

44.7.0.en: 21 “Remember these, O Jacob and Israel; for thou art my servant: I have formed thee; thou art my servant: O Israel, thou shalt not be forgotten of me. 22 I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee.” 23 Sing, O ye heavens; for the LORD hath done it: shout, ye lower parts of the earth: break forth into singing, ye mountains, O forest, and every tree therein: for the LORD hath redeemed Jacob, and glorified himself in Israel. 24 Thus saith the LORD, thy redeemer, and he that formed thee from the womb: “I am the LORD that maketh all things; that stretcheth forth the heavens alone; that spreadeth abroad the earth. Who is with me? 25 That frustrateth the tokens of the liars, and maketh diviners mad; that turneth wise men backward, and maketh their knowledge foolish; 26 That confirmeth the word of his servant, and performeth the counsel of his messengers; that saith of Jerusalem, She shall be inhabited; and of the cities of Judah, Ye shall be built, and I will raise up the decayed places thereof.”

44.7.1.en: He highlighted the vanity of idol worship or withdrawal from God, not for abstract rational criticism, but to stir the soul and urge it to accept the saving work of God, which centers on the following:

44.7.2.en: a. The establishment of God’s people: “Remember these, O Jacob and Israel; for thou art my servant” [21]... We have become the new Israel who worship God.

44.7.3.en: b. Our belonging to Him: “thou art mine” [21]; we are not only His creation and His people, but God takes pride in us as His children, belonging to Him.

44.7.4.en: c. Not being forgotten by Him [21].

44.8.0.en: d. We enjoy forgiveness of sins however dense they may be: “I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee” [22].

44.9.0.en: e. He grants the soul (the heavens) praise, and the body (the earth) a shout of joy, and our energies (the mountains) singing, and everything within us becomes like trees glorifying God [23].

44.10.0.en: 27 That saith to the deep, Be dry, and I will dry up thy rivers: 28 That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: and saith of Jerusalem, She shall be built; and to the temple, Thou shalt be founded.

44.11.0.en: About 220 years before, God declared what would be accomplished by the hand of Cyrus the pagan for the building of Jerusalem and the founding of the temple according to God’s good pleasure: “That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: and saith of Jerusalem, She shall be built; and to the temple, Thou shalt be founded” [28]. Here for the first time the name “Cyrus” is mentioned explicitly; its meaning in Persian is “sun”; and in Aramaic “shepherd”; some see that “my shepherd” was a title of some kings of the Middle East anciently.

44.11.1.en: The Jewish historian Josephus mentions that Cyrus read his name in Isaiah 220 years before and wanted to fulfill what was stated about him (see Ezra 1:2; 2 Chr 36:23).

44.11.2.en: What does He mean by saying: “That saith to the deep, Be dry, and I will dry up thy rivers” [27]?

44.11.3.en: a. He portrays Jerusalem as a deep of water and a river in which the temple cannot yet be established, according to human thought, because the Jews had lost their hope completely during the Babylonian captivity, but God, the Almighty and Caring, dries up the deeps and rivers, fulfilling His promises to us.

44.11.4.en: b. Perhaps He points here to the crossing of the Sea of Suph and the river Jordan to affirm that He is able to bring them across from captivity and return them to the land of promise.

44.11.5.en: c. Perhaps He pointed to Cyrus, who crossed the Euphrates and stormed the kingdom of Babylon.
